This applies RV-25.

findings.finding: Two clarifications before closure. First, t-s20 performs no effect: it consumes the CommitReceipt t-s16 established, so the checker must keep what the receipt records (eff-local-canonical-cas, HAPPENED) apart from the transitions that consume it (t-s16, t-s20) and never credit t-s20 with the effect. The transitions sat inside the when clause, and the checker used one effect and one PONR field for both the transition and the receipt. Second, 'exactly one per dimension' was unstated: rules are additive conjunctions, not exclusive variants, and exclusivity holds within a selector partition. The held reservation was also still a generic 'reservation' beside the consumed and released ones.
changes: The binding grammar states BindingSet(record) = common_bindings ∪ the bindings of every rule whose complete when predicate holds. Within a rule the selectors AND; across rules the matches add up; rules on the same selectors form a partition, in which every context resolves to exactly one rule (an RO AcceptanceReceipt inherits both its path rule and its READ_ONLY rule).

Each rule is {when, provenance, bindings, open}. Provenance lists the transitions a rule covers, outside the when clause, and never decides whether a rule holds, so a record's bindings can't depend on which transition consumes it. obj-26 reads as you wrote it: (SL, eff-local-canonical-cas, HAPPENED) with provenance t-s16 and t-s20; (REMOTE, eff-local-sequence-ref, HAPPENED) with t-s17; (SL, eff-local-canonical-cas, EXPECTED_OLD_STALE) with t-s18.

The checker's situations keep the transition (its role: mints, proves or consumes; its own effect and PONR flag) apart from the record's facts (path, effect, effect_result, finalization class, at_ponr, established_by). A transition proves an effect only where Chapter 0 names it as its own; a consumer takes its receipt's facts from the transition upstream that established them, so t-s20 sees t-s16's receipt. The PONR requirement comes from that transition too.

New check inventory.provenance: no rule selects on a transition; a transition that names an effect establishes its result; a consumer's facts come from an upstream transition that established them; every provenance list is exact. inventory.contexts covers intents as well as receipts and reports partitions.
reservation is renamed reservation_held; held, consumed and released are three binding facts.

Four new planted defects (your RV-25 test by the when clause, a transition used as a selector, a consumer missing from provenance, and a Chapter 0 copy crediting t-s20 with the effect) and updated messages for the rest.

findings.finding: A consumer's facts were proved for some way into its state, not every way. upstream() returns the establishing transitions it finds and drops any way in that never passes one, so a consumer reachable both through t-s16 and through a way with no proof would still be credited with t-s16's receipt, and the checks would pass. Chapter 0 has no such way today: on its path, COMMITTED is entered only by t-s16 on SL, STAGED only by t-s22, PUBLISHED only by t-s33, HALTED_AFTER_VERIFICATION through t-s28 back to t-s22, and COMMITTING only through the initiation rules.
changes: inventory.provenance requires every way into a consumer's state to pass the transition its derivation relies on: one that establishes the receipt (effect receipts), one that creates an intent for the effect a receipt records (where the effect requires one), or one that mints it (receipts transitions mint). A new planted defect runs t-s23 on SL as well, opening a way into COMMITTED from STAGING_PUBLISHING that passes no proof; the checker catches it.
